issues.legal_issue: A Collector may include distinct rates for successive years in a biennial circle-rate statement when material indicates a regular annual rise in land prices.
material_facts: The Collector issued a circle-rate statement for a two-year cycle that prescribed a 20% increase for the following year.
The challenge was confined to the Collector’s authority to prescribe that increase; the validity of the rule and the absence of material supporting the increase were not challenged.
issues.conclusion: The Collector was competent to prescribe a different rate for the following year in the biennial statement, provided material indicated a regular pattern of annual price increases; the circular was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 340-A(a) of the U.P. Stamp Rules, 1942 requires the Collector to supply the circle-rate statement biennially, meaning once every two years, but does not prohibit different rates for the two years. Where material indicates a regular annual rise in land prices, the Collector may reflect that rise in the statement. The statement is only prima facie guidance, not a final determination of market value. State of Punjab v. Mohabir Singh, (1996) 1 SCC 609, supports the principle that such guidelines are prima facie material and must not displace the statutory assessment of true market value.

predicates.stamp_duty_circle_rate_challenge: A party challenged a circle-rate determination used in assessing stamp duty on a property instrument.
predicates.biennial_rate_statement_contains_future_: The Collector supplied a circle-rate statement for a two-year cycle that listed a rate for the following year distinct from the current year's rate.
predicates.material_indicated_regular_annual_price_: Material before the Collector indicated a regular pattern of annual increases in land prices.

issues.definition: When a stamp-duty circle-rate challenge concerns a biennial statement listing a future-year rate and material indicates regular annual price increases, the Collector may prescribe distinct rates for successive years.

issues.legal_issue: A circle rate is only a prima facie guide to market value, and an affected party may contest the actual value in the Collector’s inquiry following a referral.
material_facts: The purchasers’ stated sale consideration was below the applicable circle rate, and they paid additional stamp duty by reference to that rate.
After registering the instrument, the registering authority referred it to the Collector, who issued a notice seeking a further amount based on the increased rate.
The purchasers could contest the valuation and seek to prove the actual market value in the proceedings before the Collector.
issues.conclusion: The circle rate did not finally determine the property’s market value or prevent the purchasers from contesting it. The notice and circular were valid, and the purchasers could prove the contrary valuation before the Collector.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 47-A(1)–(3) of the Indian Stamp Act, as applicable in Uttar Pradesh, provide for referral to the Collector where the stated value is below the prescribed minimum or the registering officer has reason to believe the value is not truly stated; the Collector then determines market value after giving the parties a reasonable opportunity to be heard and conducting an inquiry. Rule 340-A supplies circle rates as guidance, not as a final valuation. State of Punjab v. Mohabir Singh, (1996) 1 SCC 609, is relied on for the principle that guidelines are prima facie material and cannot substitute for assessment of the true market value in the individual case.

predicates.stamp_valuation_referral_proceeding: A registering authority referred a property instrument to the Collector for determination of market value and proper stamp duty.
predicates.instrument_value_below_circle_rate: The value stated in the instrument was below the applicable circle rate.
predicates.affected_party_can_contest_valuation_bef: The affected party was given an opportunity to contest the valuation and present evidence of the property’s actual market value before the Collector.

issues.definition: In a stamp-valuation referral where the instrument value is below the circle rate and the affected party can contest valuation before the Collector, the circle rate remains nonfinal and actual market value may be proved.
